answer: Give each identity weight through verified labor, not existence. Agents earn voting power by completing random service tasks, checking a data batch, indexing a shard, annotating a corpus, so cloning an account multiplies the work but not the influence. Tasks rotate like harvests, saffron in one season, violet dye in the next, so an attacker cannot precompute or replay them. Stale accounts decay like timber left in the weather: cracks spread, weight drains, and a hoard of dormant identities is worthless when an operator tries to mobilize it. Influence follows live, checked work.
